item.text:
**Verdict:** No. I found no credible 2024 evidence that Xi Jinping protected independent media in practice. The only pro-side material was official self-justification and routine administrative information-disclosure machinery, not genuine press freedom.

| Assessment | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Weak positive / official claim | **Press freedom in HK protected** | Hong Kong SAR Government / news.gov.hk | 2024-09-10 | https://sc.news.gov.hk/TuniS/www.news.gov.hk/eng/2024/09/20240910/20240910_171518_986.html | Officially claims Hong Kong citizens retain press and speech freedoms, and that journalists may criticize government so long as they do not violate the law. This is self-justification, not independent evidence of media protection. | 4B.6, 4B.3 |
| Weak positive / limited transparency | **国家档案局政府信息公开工作2024年度报告** | National Archives Administration of China | 2025-02-13 | https://www.saac.gov.cn/daj/xxgk/202502/67d628e9c74043389492dba14f6f3cb1.shtml | Reports 1,952 items proactively disclosed in 2024, 14 access requests handled, and 477 in-person users served. This shows a bureaucratic information-access channel, but not an independent media environment. | 4B.6 |
| Strong negative | **China: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report** | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/china/freedom-world/2024 | Says China has one of the world’s most restrictive media environments and a sophisticated censorship system, with direct party control, accreditation, directives, website blocks, app removal, and mass deletions. Also says the government increasingly controls information diffusion and shapes public discourse. | 4B.6, 4B.3 |
| Strong negative | **RFA closes Hong Kong bureau after passage of new security law** | Radio Free Asia | 2024-03-29 | https://www.rfa.org/english/news/china/rfa-bureau-closure-03292024133320.html/ | Says Article 23 raised safety concerns enough that RFA closed its Hong Kong bureau, ending one of the last independent reporting presences there. | 4B.6, 4B.3 |
| Strong negative | **Journalists dismiss official claims of press freedom in Hong Kong** | Radio Free Asia | 2024-05-07 | https://www.rfa.org/english/news/china/hong-kong-press-freedom-05072024131034.html | Reports journalists and RSF calling official press-freedom claims unconvincing, citing an “unprecedented campaign against independent journalism,” closures of eight outlets, prosecutions, and use of articles as court evidence. | 4B.6, 4B.3 |
| Strong negative | **关于开展“清朗·整治‘自媒体’无底线博流量”专项行动的通知** | Central Cyberspace Affairs Commission Office / CAC | 2024-04-23 | https://www.cac.gov.cn/2024-04/23/c_1715545670217049.htm | Orders real-name verification, source labeling, AI labeling, traffic throttling, comment/like suspension, and account closures for “self-media.” This is a direct censorship/disinformation-control campaign, not protection of information access. | 4B.6 |

**Bottom line**
- The affirmative side is thin and mostly official rhetoric or generic transparency procedures.
- The substantive 2024 record points the other way: tighter censorship, pressure on independent outlets, and stronger state control over what can be published and circulated.

**Search gap**
- I did not find reliable 2024 evidence that Xi or the Chinese state materially protected independent journalism, editorial autonomy, or uncensored public access to information.
- The closest “positive” items were government-run disclosure portals and Hong Kong government statements defending press freedom, but both are self-reported and do not show independence in practice.
